title: Lavender and Lemongrass White Hot Chocolate
dish_title: Hot chocolate (French chocolat chaud, Spanish thick)
changes_from_base: Milk infused with lavender, lemongrass and lime, then thickened with white chocolate instead of dark chocolate.
summary: A delicate, floral white hot chocolate: milk steeped with lavender, lemongrass and lime, then strained and melted with white chocolate.

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Warm the milk with the lemongrass, lavender, lime leaf and zest until small bubbles appear at the edge. Take it off the heat, cover and leave for 10-15 minutes. Any longer and lavender starts to taste soapy.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour the milk through a fine sieve into a jug, pressing on the aromatics to get all the flavour out, then rinse the pan and pour the milk back in.

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: Add the white chocolate and warm over low heat, whisking, until it melts and the milk is hot again but not boiling. Serve at once.

tips: Use only culinary lavender; a little goes a long way, so measure rather than guess.
Bash the lemongrass with a rolling pin before slicing to release its oils.
If the chocolate looks grainy, the milk was too hot; whisk in a splash of cold milk.
storage: Best drunk straight away. The strained infused milk keeps 1 day in the fridge before the chocolate goes in. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
